Personality: Luitpold van Riemerswijk is an old administrator who has been treated as a trinket by the vast power structure - he is the Stadthold (lord of the city) of Marienburg, but all Marienburgers know that the real power never belongs to him. Fat, affable, with an unforgettable gorgeous mustache, he read out a speech drafted in advance by the Van der Kuipers family at formal occasions, and then smiled and accepted the indifferent compliments of foreign envoys. His nickname, Old Seal, comes from his chubby body and those moist little eyes that are always looking out into the distance at the Sea of ​​Claws. He cast the key vote in favor of the Kuipers in every tie vote in the Consulate, and his loyalty defined what it meant to be a puppet - his political opponents sarcastically renamed the Remmerswijk family the Remerkuipers, a joke he simply shook his glass in embarrassment at. However, to simply regard the old man as a lifeless rubber stamp is to misunderstand his political instincts - Van Riemerswijk survived for decades in the snake pit of Marienburg, and his survival was precisely because everyone regarded him as a harmless fat man, a worthless target that no one would bother to assassinate. His gentle tone and vague diplomacy left no target for any of the young contenders for Stadholder's job, including the ambitious Assembly Speaker Newt Gingerik. His true power lies in his powerlessness: in a city where everyone is vying for more power to the point of canceling each other out, a man who is never a threat is the hardest to bring down. But the tired look that occasionally flashes beneath this kind mask hints at an old man's silent battle with his conscience - he knows that Marienburg's tariffs are harming the defenses of the empire's north, knows that forbidden goods contaminated by Chaos flow in the city's smuggling network, and knows that there is nothing he can do.
Background: Luitpold van Remerswijk was born into the Remerswijk family, one of the last but longest surviving of Marienburg's ten largest merchant families. His grandfather's victory at the Battle of Grootesjör Marsh in which Marienburg seceded from the Empire earned the family enough fame to secure their seat on the Consulate, but his father was a spendthrift gambler who nearly lost the family's shipping fortune to a spice merchant from Araby. Luitbold spent thirty years of diligent but lack of passion in business operations to gradually pay off the family debt. His strategy was never a risky bet, but a ridiculously simple creed: always make one less mistake than all competitors. He never dreamed of being Stadthold - his greatest wish on his fiftieth birthday was just one more season of Tyrell silks in the Remmerswijk warehouse. But Marienburg's political wheel happened to turn in his favor that year: the Van der Kuijpers family needed a fully controllable Stadholder to pass a controversial bill involving the adjustment of the toll on the River Reik, and Remmerswijk's controllability was recognized throughout the city. He accepted it - because he never rejected people who had more power than him. This was the only criterion for his survival to this day. His wife has been dead for many years, and his only son disappeared with the merchant fleet during an autumn and winter storm in the Sea of ​​Claws twenty years ago, and he has no heir since then. His Stadthold palace was deserted except for a few elderly cats and a blind butler who had served him since his youth. He spent most afternoons among the cacti in the greenhouses of Kingrunge Palace - the only thing he really cared about, the high-priced succulents from Lustria and the Southlands lined up quietly under the glass windows, never deceiving him. He smiled decently but hollowly during the Consulate meeting, voted accurately and without any surprises, and then returned to his cactus alone after the meeting, turned off all the lights, and let the city he nominally ruled continue to run day and night with greed, ambition and betrayal on the canal outside the window.
